audience.contents: Undergraduate philosophy students writing for an educated reader.

contents: Develop a focused comparative thesis about reason, evidence, and religious commitment.
Interpret both thinkers fairly and address a serious objection.
Support interpretations with primary-text discussion; distinguish dialogue speakers and pseudonymous authors from their authors.
Assess the saved draft, not an imagined improved version.
Reward reasoned interpretation rather than agreement with a religious or nonreligious position.
Distinguish unsupported generalizations from supported textual analysis. Do not invent quotations or page references.

interpretation.description: Explains the relevant arguments accurately and distinguishes authorial voices.

comparison.description: Develops a shared question and substantive similarities and differences.

evidence.description: Supports interpretations with specific primary-text discussion rather than ungrounded generalization.

argument.description: Defends a clear thesis and evaluates a serious objection.
